tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What was the woman’s first impression of the apartment?

options.A: It was spacious and tranquil.
options.B: It was warm and comfortable.
options.C: It was shabby and solitary.
options.D: It was tiny and noisy.

questions.cn: 女士对这间公寓的第一印象是什么？

optionsCn.A: 它宽敞而宁静。
optionsCn.B: 它温暖而舒适。
optionsCn.C: 它破旧而孤单。
optionsCn.D: 它狭小而吵闹。

questions.stem: Why does the woman say she is going to sound like an idiot?

options.A: She no longer hates people talking loudly in the dorm.
options.B: She misses her roommates she used to complain about.
options.C: She begins to enjoy the movies she once found irritating.
options.D: She finds the crowded dorm as cozy as her new apartment.

questions.cn: 女士为什么说她这话说出来会像个傻瓜？

optionsCn.A: 她不再讨厌宿舍里大声说话的人。
optionsCn.B: 她想念自己过去常抱怨的室友。
optionsCn.C: 她开始享受曾经觉得烦人的电影。
optionsCn.D: 她觉得拥挤的宿舍和新公寓一样温馨。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man when he left the dormitory to live on his own?

options.A: He found the apartment perfectly furnished.
options.B: He had a feeling of despair and frustration.
options.C: He had a similar feeling to the woman.
options.D: He felt the new place was like paradise.

questions.cn: 关于男士离开宿舍独自生活时的情况，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 他觉得公寓家具配备得很完美。
optionsCn.B: 他感到绝望和沮丧。
optionsCn.C: 他有与女士相似的感受。
optionsCn.D: 他觉得新住处像天堂。

questions.stem: What does the man say he can’t wait to do?

options.A: Go to see the woman’s apartment.
options.B: Make a phone call to his parents.
options.C: Buy some furniture for the woman.
options.D: Decorate the woman’s apartment.

questions.cn: 男士说他迫不及待想做什么？

optionsCn.A: 去看看女士的公寓。
optionsCn.B: 给父母打个电话。
optionsCn.C: 给女士买些家具。
optionsCn.D: 为女士布置公寓。

lines.t: Hi, Lily, how’s the new apartment?
lines.cn: 嗨，莉莉，新公寓怎么样？

lines.t: It’s okay.
lines.cn: 还行吧。

lines.t: What?
lines.cn: 什么？

lines.t: How can it be just okay when last week you were thrilled about the place and kept posting photos of it online?
lines.cn: 上周你还为这地方兴奋不已、不停在网上发照片，怎么可能只是“还行”？

lines.t: Well, last week when I moved in, the apartment seemed cozy, just the right size for one person.
lines.cn: 嗯，上周刚搬进来时，公寓看起来温馨，一个人住大小正合适。

lines.t: But now it just seems tiny, shabby and solitary.
lines.cn: 可现在它只是显得又小又破，还孤单。

lines.t: Ah, that’s the problem.
lines.cn: 啊，问题就在这儿。

lines.t: You miss your roommates from university, don’t you?
lines.cn: 你想大学时的室友了，是不是？

lines.t: I’m going to sound like an idiot, because I used to complain to you all the time about how crowded our dormitory room was, and about all the things they did to irritate me, like watching movies late at night without headphones, or talking loudly early in the morning.
lines.cn: 我这话说出来会像个傻瓜，因为我以前总跟你抱怨我们宿舍多挤，抱怨她们做的那些让我烦的事，比如深夜不戴耳机看电影，或者大清早就大声说话。

lines.t: But now I miss them terribly.
lines.cn: 但现在我特别想她们。

lines.t: Of course you do.
lines.cn: 那当然。

lines.t: That’s perfectly normal.
lines.cn: 这太正常了。

lines.t: When I got my first place I remember thinking I couldn’t wait to live by myself and get away from my juvenile roommates and all their annoying habits.
lines.cn: 我搬进第一处住处时，记得自己想着终于能一个人住、摆脱那些幼稚的室友和她们各种讨厌的习惯，简直等不及。

lines.t: But then I began missing them and feeling lonely and thinking that our dormitory was like paradise, even though there were six of us guys in one small room.
lines.cn: 但后来我开始想他们、感到孤单，觉得我们的宿舍就像天堂，尽管我们六个男生挤在一间小屋里。

lines.t: I thought it was just me who felt like that.
lines.cn: 我以为只有我这样想。

lines.t: Look, you lived at home with us, and then you had three roommates, and this is your first time living alone.
lines.cn: 你看，你一直和我们住家里，然后有三个室友，而这是你第一次独自生活。

lines.t: So it’s hard.
lines.cn: 所以会难。

lines.t: But your first apartment is a milestone in your life, and you should celebrate it.
lines.cn: 但你的第一间公寓是人生中的一个里程碑，你应该庆祝一下。

lines.t: Tell me about the apartment.
lines.cn: 跟我说说这公寓吧。

lines.t: Actually, it’s not bad.
lines.cn: 其实，还不错。

lines.t: In fact, it’s pretty adorable, now that I have decorated it and it has everything I need.
lines.cn: 事实上，挺可爱的——我布置过之后，而且我需要的东西都有。

lines.t: I have a kitchen to cook in and a bathroom all to myself, and then another room with my bed at one end, and a sofa, a small table and chairs at the other end.
lines.cn: 我有厨房可以做饭，有独用的浴室，还有另一个房间，一头是我的床，另一头是沙发、小桌子和椅子。

lines.t: That does sound adorable and I can’t wait to see it, and neither can mom and dad.
lines.cn: 听起来确实很可爱，我迫不及待想看看，爸妈也一样。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn from the conversation about the man?

options.A: He works as a literary critic.
options.B: He hosts an educational program.
options.C: He has initiated a university reform.
options.D: He has published a book recently.

questions.cn: 从对话中关于男士我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 他是一名文学评论家。
optionsCn.B: 他主持一档教育节目。
optionsCn.C: 他发起了一场大学改革。
optionsCn.D: 他最近出版了一本书。

questions.stem: What does the man believe is the problem with the current American system of higher education?

options.A: It fails to keep up with the radical changes of society.
options.B: It fails to ensure universities get sufficient resources.
options.C: It has not prepared young people for the job market.
options.D: It has not fostered the growth of the arts disciplines.

questions.cn: 男士认为美国现行高等教育体制的问题是什么？

optionsCn.A: 它未能跟上社会的剧烈变化。
optionsCn.B: 它未能确保大学获得充足资源。
optionsCn.C: 它没有让年轻人为就业市场做好准备。
optionsCn.D: 它没有促进艺术学科的发展。

questions.stem: How should the education budget be allocated according to the man?

options.A: More of the budget should go to science and technology.
options.B: The underfunded music discipline should be prioritized.
options.C: Subdisciplines like sculpture should get more funding.
options.D: Literature should get as much funding as engineering.

questions.cn: 根据男士，教育预算应当如何分配？

optionsCn.A: 更多预算应投向科学和技术。
optionsCn.B: 资金不足的音乐学科应优先考虑。
optionsCn.C: 像雕塑这样的分支学科应获得更多资金。
optionsCn.D: 文学应获得与工程同样多的资金。

questions.stem: What does the woman say the arts can do?

options.A: Build a prosperous nation.
options.B: Make skilled professionals.
options.C: Create ingenious artists.
options.D: Cultivate better citizens.

questions.cn: 女士说艺术能做什么？

optionsCn.A: 建设繁荣的国家。
optionsCn.B: 培养熟练的专业人才。
optionsCn.C: 造就天才的艺术家。
optionsCn.D: 培育更好的公民。

lines.t: Welcome to our program Book Talk.
lines.cn: 欢迎收听我们的节目《书谈》。

lines.t: Our guest today is Frank Jones, a critic of our education system, and the author of a new book, How to Reform Our Universities.
lines.cn: 今天的嘉宾是弗兰克·琼斯，我们教育体制的批评者，也是新书《如何改革我们的大学》的作者。

lines.t: Hello, Susan.
lines.cn: 你好，苏珊。

lines.t: Frank, you support radically changing universities in America?
lines.cn: 弗兰克，你支持对美国大学进行彻底改革？

lines.t: Yes, I believe that the purpose of higher education is to prepare young people to enter the workforce, and that our current system fails to do this.
lines.cn: 是的，我相信高等教育的目的是让年轻人做好进入职场的准备，而我们现行的体制做不到这一点。

lines.t: We’re allocating too many resources to disciplines that don’t match the needs of employers.
lines.cn: 我们把太多资源分配给了与雇主需求不匹配的学科。

lines.t: I think your attitude to education is a bit cynical, Frank.
lines.cn: 弗兰克，我觉得你对教育的态度有点愤世嫉俗。

lines.t: Surely the purpose of university is to prepare young people to participate fully in civic life, rather than just to find well-paid jobs.
lines.cn: 大学的目的想必是让年轻人做好充分参与公民生活的准备，而不只是找到高薪工作吧。

lines.t: Susan, many young graduates struggle to find any job, let alone a good one.
lines.cn: 苏珊，许多年轻毕业生连工作都难找，更别说好工作了。

lines.t: The job market is grim, particularly for students who study the arts.
lines.cn: 就业市场很严峻，对学艺术的学生尤其如此。

lines.t: I agree that it isn’t easy for young people to find work, but you propose closing down all departments that aren’t directly related to science and technology.
lines.cn: 我同意年轻人找工作不容易，但你提议关掉所有与科技没有直接关系的院系。

lines.t: Is that really the solution?
lines.cn: 这真的是解决办法吗？

lines.t: You’re overstating my point.
lines.cn: 你夸大了我的观点。

lines.t: My argument is that we need to use more of our budget on areas like science and engineering.
lines.cn: 我的论点是，我们需要把更多预算用在科学和工程这类领域。

lines.t: To do that, we need to take money from subjects like literature and music.
lines.cn: 要做到这一点，我们得从文学、音乐这类学科里抽出钱来。

lines.t: But the arts have value.
lines.cn: 但艺术是有价值的。

lines.t: They’re an important part of our culture.
lines.cn: 它们是我们文化的重要部分。

lines.t: Studying literature or music or sculpture might not result in a job in that area, but it helps young people to think about the world in a deeper way, which makes them better citizens and makes for a better society.
lines.cn: 学文学、音乐或雕塑也许不会带来这一领域的就业，但它帮助年轻人更深入地思考世界，从而让他们成为更好的公民，也造就更好的社会。

lines.t: I agree that the arts are valuable to society, but it’s naive to think that not only the most talented, but all students should study them at university level.
lines.cn: 我同意艺术对社会有价值，但如果认为不仅最有才华的学生、而是所有学生都该在大学层面学艺术，那就太天真了。

lines.t: The arts are very competitive, and most graduates will end up with a great deal of debt, obtaining a degree that has little value on the job market.
lines.cn: 艺术领域竞争非常激烈，大多毕业生最终会背上大笔债务，换来一个在就业市场上价值甚微的学位。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the feeling that one doesn’t have time to think anymore?

options.A: It is quite common.
options.B: It is rarely noticed.
options.C: It seldom annoys people.
options.D: It occurs when one is alone.

questions.cn: 关于“再没时间思考”这种感觉，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它相当普遍。
optionsCn.B: 它很少被察觉。
optionsCn.C: 它很少让人烦恼。
optionsCn.D: 它只在一个独处时出现。

questions.stem: What trait do all great professionals share?

options.A: Seeing things in black and white.
options.B: Engaging in regular contemplation.
options.C: Having a special understanding of creativity.
options.D: Knowing how to make their mental batteries work.

questions.cn: 所有杰出的专业人士都共有哪种特质？

optionsCn.A: 以非黑即白的方式看事情。
optionsCn.B: 进行定期的沉思。
optionsCn.C: 对创造力有特别的理解。
optionsCn.D: 懂得如何让心力发挥作用。

questions.stem: What do some researchers believe is conducive to creative ideas?

options.A: Engaging in intense activity.
options.B: Fantasizing in one’s down time.
options.C: Working on a particular project.
options.D: Reflecting during one’s relaxation.

questions.cn: 一些研究者认为什么有助于产生创意？

optionsCn.A: 从事高强度活动。
optionsCn.B: 在空闲时幻想。
optionsCn.C: 投入某个特定项目。
optionsCn.D: 在放松时反思。

lines.t: Do you ever have the annoying feeling that you don’t have time to really think anymore?
lines.cn: 你有没有过那种恼人的感觉：自己再也没有时间真正思考了？

lines.t: You are not alone.
lines.cn: 你并不孤单。

lines.t: A variety of factors have conspired to rob us of time for reflection about ourselves and our lives.
lines.cn: 各种因素合谋剥夺了我们反思自己和人生的时间。

lines.t: Today, our preoccupied minds are rarely silent.
lines.cn: 如今，我们思绪纷杂的头脑很少安静。

lines.t: The average person receives hundreds of texts and voice messages a day, and holidays for many of us are action-packed weeks more likely full of family activities than opportunities for tranquility and contemplation.
lines.cn: 普通人每天收到数百条短信和语音信息；对我们许多人来说，假期是安排得满满当当的几周，更可能塞满家庭活动，而不是享受宁静与沉思的机会。

lines.t: Regular reflection, however, underlies all great professionals.
lines.cn: 然而，定期反思是所有杰出专业人士的基础。

lines.t: It’s a prerequisite for you to recharge your mental batteries, see things in a new light and tap into your creativity.
lines.cn: 它是你为自己充电、以新视角看事物、激发创造力的前提。

lines.t: Almost all of the great advisors that I have studied have found ways to get away from it all and contemplate their life and work.
lines.cn: 我研究过的几乎所有伟大的顾问都找到了抽身事外、思考自己生活与工作的方式。

lines.t: Some researchers in the field of creativity, in fact, believe that insight occurs during the reflection and relaxation that follows a period of intense activity.
lines.cn: 事实上，创造力领域的一些研究者认为，洞察力产生于高强度活动之后随之而来的反思与放松之中。

lines.t: Schedule time for reflection about your work or a particular project you’re engaged in.
lines.cn: 为反思你的工作或正在投入的某个项目安排时间。

lines.t: I usually block out half an hour.
lines.cn: 我通常留出半小时。

lines.t: Don’t answer the phone.
lines.cn: 不要接电话。

lines.t: Push your papers to the side.
lines.cn: 把文件推到一边。

lines.t: Sketch, make lists, draw “mind maps” of ideas that come to you.
lines.cn: 随手画、列清单、把想到的点子画成“思维导图”。

lines.t: At the end, write down any emerging ideas.
lines.cn: 最后，把任何浮现的想法写下来。

lines.t: When you’re alone, stop worrying and think.
lines.cn: 独处的时候，别再担忧，去思考。

lines.t: A lot of our down time is spent worrying about troublesome things in our lives or fantasizing about how we’d like our lives to be.
lines.cn: 我们的很多空闲时间都花在为生活中的烦心事担忧，或幻想希望自己的生活是什么样。

lines.t: Revisit things during moments of relaxation after a period of intense work.
lines.cn: 在高强度工作之后的一段放松时光里，重新审视那些事情。

lines.t: This is when we are the most creative.
lines.cn: 这正是我们最有创造力的时候。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 4 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about Colorado before it became a state?

options.A: Farmers helped Native Americans grow crops.
options.B: There were expansive university campuses.
options.C: There existed post offices.
options.D: Migrants found gold there.

questions.cn: 关于成为州之前的科罗拉多，文章说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 农民帮助美洲原住民种植庄稼。
optionsCn.B: 有占地广阔的大学校园。
optionsCn.C: 已经有邮局。
optionsCn.D: 移民在那里发现了黄金。

questions.stem: How did the postal service contribute to America’s westward expansion?

options.A: It helped to boost the economy in the American West.
options.B: It provided job opportunities for many gold seekers.
options.C: It extended the influence of the federal government.
options.D: It kept people in the deserts and plains connected.

questions.cn: 邮政服务如何促进了美国的西进？

optionsCn.A: 它帮助提振了美国西部的经济。
optionsCn.B: 它为许多寻金者提供了工作机会。
optionsCn.C: 它扩大了联邦政府的影响力。
optionsCn.D: 它让沙漠和平原上的人们保持联络。

questions.stem: What did the federal government do to meet the increasing demand for the postal service in the West?

options.A: It employed Native Americans to work as postmen.
options.B: It commissioned private wagons to carry the mail.
options.C: It subsidized the locals who acted as postmasters.
options.D: It centralized postal services in its remote areas.

questions.cn: 联邦政府做了什么来满足西部日益增长的邮政需求？

optionsCn.A: 它雇用美洲原住民当邮递员。
optionsCn.B: 它委托私人马车运送邮件。
optionsCn.C: 它补贴充当邮政局长的当地人。
optionsCn.D: 它把偏远地区的邮政服务集中起来。

questions.stem: What did Mr. Blevins do to study the history of the US postal service?

options.A: He analyzed interactive maps of mail routes.
options.B: He read a large collection of books on the topic.
options.C: He examined its historical trends with data science.
options.D: He collected data about its impact on local business.

questions.cn: 布莱文斯先生做了什么来研究美国邮政史？

optionsCn.A: 他分析了邮路的互动地图。
optionsCn.B: 他读了一大批关于该主题的书籍。
optionsCn.C: 他用数据科学考察其历史趋势。
optionsCn.D: 他收集了关于其对当地商业影响的数据。

lines.t: Even before Colorado was a state, it had post offices.
lines.cn: 早在科罗拉多成为州之前，它就已经有邮局了。

lines.t: The first opened in 1859, in a settlement founded by migrants searching for gold.
lines.cn: 第一家邮局于 1859 年开办，位于一个由寻金移民建立的定居点。

lines.t: Life could be unpredictable at West- gold failed to appear, drought ruined farmers and settlers clashed with Native Americans.
lines.cn: 西部的生活可能难以预料——黄金没有出现，旱灾毁了农民，定居者与美洲原住民发生冲突。

lines.t: On the settlement’s location now stands a sprawling university campus.
lines.cn: 当年那个定居点的位置上，如今坐落着一片占地广阔大学校园。

lines.t: Amid all the changes, one feature remained constant- the postal service.
lines.cn: 在所有这些变化之中，有一项始终未变——邮政服务。

lines.t: The maps tracing America’s westward expansion are telling.
lines.cn: 勾勒美国西进的地图很能说明问题。

lines.t: In 1864, there were few postal branches on land controlled by Native Americans, which still accounted for most of the West.
lines.cn: 1864 年，在美洲原住民控制的土地上几乎没有什么邮局分支，而当时西部大部分土地仍由原住民控制。

lines.t: Over the next 25 years, post offices grew quickly.
lines.cn: 在接下来的 25 年里，邮局数量迅速增长。

lines.t: Colonization of the West could be regarded as a result of big government rather than pioneers.
lines.cn: 西部的殖民化或许可以被看作大政府、而不是拓荒者的结果。

lines.t: As federal subsidies and land grants tempted people into the deserts and plains, the post kept them connected.
lines.cn: 联邦补贴和土地赠予把人们吸引到沙漠和平原，而邮政让他们保持联结。

lines.t: In the mid-19th century, the Post Office Department was far from a centralized bureaucracy.
lines.cn: 19 世纪中叶，邮政部远非一个中央集权的官僚机构。

lines.t: To keep up with migration patterns, postal services were added to existing businesses.
lines.cn: 为了跟上移民流动的节奏，邮政服务被增设到已有的商铺之中。

lines.t: The federal government commissioned private wagons to carry the mail.
lines.cn: 联邦政府委托私人马车运送邮件。

lines.t: Short-term contracts were granted to local businessmen to act as postmasters.
lines.cn: 短期合同授予当地商人，让他们充当邮政局长。

lines.t: These partnerships enabled the mail to quickly follow migrants, helping knit together remote parts of the country.
lines.cn: 这些合作关系使邮件能迅速跟随移民，帮助把偏远地区缝合在一起。

lines.t: Mr. Blevins, a digital historian, wrote a book on the history of the US postal service; he used data science to analyze historical trends.
lines.cn: 数字历史学家布莱文斯先生写过一本关于美国邮政史的著作；他用数据科学分析历史趋势。

lines.t: Most strikingly, he built an accompanying website, complete with interactive maps.
lines.cn: 最引人注目的是，他还搭建了一个配套网站，配有互动地图。

lines.t: They show readers how, within a generation, the postal service helped colonize a continent.
lines.cn: 它们向读者展示，在一代人的时间里，邮政服务如何帮助殖民了一整个大陆。

lines.t: These online interactive maps illustrate the formative power of snail mail.
lines.cn: 这些在线互动地图展现了传统平信的塑造之力。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 5 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say the new study suggests?

options.A: Higher levels of anxiety may improve people’s memory.
options.B: Some experiences are easier to remember than others.
options.C: Most people tend to remember things selectively.
options.D: Simple things may leave a deep impression on one’s memory.

questions.cn: 讲话者说这项新研究显示了什么？

optionsCn.A: 更高的焦虑水平可能改善人的记忆。
optionsCn.B: 有些经历比其他经历更容易记住。
optionsCn.C: 大多数人倾向于有选择地记住事情。
optionsCn.D: 简单的事情可能在记忆中留下深刻印象。

questions.stem: What did researchers do first in the new study?

options.A: They classified the participants’ mindset.
options.B: They showed some photos to the participants.
options.C: They measured the participants’ anxiety levels.
options.D: They tested the size of the participants’ vocabulary.

questions.cn: 在这项新研究中，研究者首先做了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们对参与者的心态进行了分类。
optionsCn.B: 他们给参与者看了一些照片。
optionsCn.C: 他们测量了参与者的焦虑水平。
optionsCn.D: 他们测试了参与者的词汇量。

questions.stem: What do we learn from previous studies about anxiety?

options.A: Anxiety has become a serious problem for an increasing number of people.
options.B: Extreme levels of anxiety can adversely affect cognitive performance.
options.C: People diagnosed with anxiety disorder may forget things selectively.
options.D: There is no direct correlation between memory and levels of anxiety.

questions.cn: 关于焦虑，我们从既有研究中了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 焦虑已成为越来越多人面临的严重问题。
optionsCn.B: 极端水平的焦虑会对认知表现产生不良影响。
optionsCn.C: 被诊断为焦虑症的人可能有选择地遗忘事情。
optionsCn.D: 记忆与焦虑水平之间没有直接关联。

lines.t: In last week’s lecture, we discussed reasons why people forget things.
lines.cn: 上次课我们讨论了人们遗忘事物的原因。

lines.t: This week, we will discuss a surprising reason why we might remember some things- anxiety.
lines.cn: 这周我们要讨论一个令人惊讶的、我们可能记住某些事的原因——焦虑。

lines.t: Think about something as simple as buying a coffee.
lines.cn: 想想买咖啡这样的小事。

lines.t: That may not seem like an experience that would make a deep impression on your memory, but anxiety could change that.
lines.cn: 那似乎不是会在记忆中留下深刻印象的经历，但焦虑可以改变这一点。

lines.t: In fact, a new study suggests that people with higher anxiety levels might remember certain information better than people with lower anxiety levels.
lines.cn: 事实上，一项新研究显示，焦虑水平较高的人可能比焦虑水平较低的人更好地记住某些信息。

lines.t: That’s because higher levels of anxiety may make people more susceptible to negative feelings, putting them in a more negative state of mind.
lines.cn: 这是因为更高水平的焦虑可能让人更容易受负面情绪影响，使他们处于更消极的心理状态。

lines.t: That in turn may make them able to better remember some events.
lines.cn: 而这又可能让他们更好地记住某些事件。

lines.t: Let’s take a closer look at that new study now.
lines.cn: 我们现在来仔细看看这项新研究。

lines.t: In the study, the researchers started by giving 80 undergraduate students an anxiety test.
lines.cn: 研究中，研究者先给 80 名本科生做了一项焦虑测试。

lines.t: The test measured the participants’ anxiety levels over the preceding two weeks.
lines.cn: 该测试测量参与者过去两周的焦虑水平。

lines.t: Then, to test memory, the participants were shown a series of neutral words, one at a time.
lines.cn: 随后，为测试记忆，参与者被逐一展示一系列中性词。

lines.t: Some of the words were printed on to photos of negative scenes, meaning images that could affect their emotions negatively, such as a photo of a car accident or a cemetery.
lines.cn: 其中一些词印在负面场景的照片上，即可能对情绪产生负面影响的图像，比如车祸或墓地的照片。

lines.t: The rest of the words were printed on to photos of neutral scenes, such as a photo of a lake or trees.
lines.cn: 其余的词印在中性场景的照片上，比如湖泊或树木的照片。

lines.t: Neutral words included words like “table” or “desk” that don’t elicit emotion.
lines.cn: 中性词包括“桌子”或“书桌”这类不引发情绪的词语。

lines.t: Later, the participants were asked to think back to the words they were shown earlier, which caused them to reenter either a negative or a neutral mindset.
lines.cn: 之后，参与者被要求回想先前看过的词，这使他们重新进入负面或中性的心态。

lines.t: The participants were then presented with another set of neutral words, and their memory of these new words was tested.
lines.cn: 随后研究者又给参与者呈现另一组中性词，并测试他们对这些新词的记忆。

lines.t: The researchers found that the new words presented to people in a negative mindset were better remembered by people with higher levels of anxiety than those with lower levels of anxiety.
lines.cn: 研究者发现，对处于负面心态的人呈现的新词，焦虑水平较高的参与者记得比焦虑水平较低的人更好。

lines.t: In other words, when highly anxious individuals took in otherwise emotionally neutral information that was presented to them, it became colored by their negative mindset, making them remember the information better.
lines.cn: 换句话说，当高度焦虑的个体接收本无情绪色彩的中性信息时，这些信息被他们的负面心态染上了色彩，从而让他们记得更牢。

lines.t: But these same effects were not seen in people with low levels of anxiety.
lines.cn: 但在焦虑水平低的人身上并未出现同样的效应。

lines.t: Previous studies have found that extreme levels of anxiety, such as those experienced by people diagnosed with an anxiety disorder, can be quite detrimental to memory and cognitive performance.
lines.cn: 既有研究发现，极端水平的焦虑——比如被诊断为焦虑症的人所经历的——可能对记忆和认知表现相当有害。

lines.t: But the highly anxious people in this study represent individuals who are managing their anxiety and for whom anxiety is not a serious problem.
lines.cn: 但本研究中的高度焦虑者代表的是那些能够管理自身焦虑、焦虑对他们并非严重问题的人。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 6 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about today’s consumers?

options.A: They compare products from different companies before making a choice.
options.B: They get information from other consumers’ postings and comments.
options.C: They lose patience when their phone call is not promptly answered.
options.D: They expect to get instantaneous responses to their inquiry.

questions.cn: 关于今天的消费者，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们会在做选择前比较不同公司的产品。
optionsCn.B: 他们从其他消费者的帖子和评论中获取信息。
optionsCn.C: 电话没被及时接听时他们会失去耐心。
optionsCn.D: 他们期待自己的询问得到即时回应。

questions.stem: How do marketers capture consumers’ attention as quickly as possible?

options.A: Giving them rewards on the spot.
options.B: Broadening their scope of interest.
options.C: Speaking directly to their emotions.
options.D: Focusing on the details of the product.

questions.cn: 营销人员如何尽可能快地抓住消费者的注意力？

optionsCn.A: 当场给他们奖励。
optionsCn.B: 拓宽他们的兴趣范围。
optionsCn.C: 直接诉诸他们的情感。
optionsCn.D: 聚焦产品的细节。

questions.stem: What does the speaker suggest marketers do to meet future challenges?

options.A: Change the rules of the game in the market every year.
options.B: Keep up with the latest technological developments.
options.C: Learn from technological innovators to do business.
options.D: Make greater efforts to build up consumers’ confidence.

questions.cn: 讲话者建议营销人员做什么来应对未来挑战？

optionsCn.A: 每年改变市场上的游戏规则。
optionsCn.B: 跟上最新的技术发展。
optionsCn.C: 向技术革新者学习如何做生意。
optionsCn.D: 付出更大努力来建立消费者的信心。

lines.t: Over the past 20 years, the internet has gradually become a dominant feature of our lives.
lines.cn: 过去 20 年里，互联网已逐渐成为我们生活的主要特征。

lines.t: It has changed how we communicate with each other, and it has definitely transformed the way we do business with each other.
lines.cn: 它改变了我们相互交流的方式，也肯定改变了我们彼此做生意的模式。

lines.t: Marketing has also changed in a number of ways.
lines.cn: 营销也在多个方面发生了变化。

lines.t: For instance, in the past, consumers had to call a phone number and patiently wait on hold, in order to get the information they wanted.
lines.cn: 例如，过去消费者必须打电话、耐心等待接通，才能得到想要的信息。

lines.t: Today, they want the information immediately.
lines.cn: 如今，他们想要信息立刻到手。

lines.t: They’ll go to the company’s social media page and post comments and questions, expecting to receive an immediate response.
lines.cn: 他们会到公司的社交媒体页面留言提问，期待立即得到回应。

lines.t: If they don’t get their questions answered soon, they’ll move on to another company that will answer them quickly.
lines.cn: 如果问题不能很快得到答复，他们就会转向另一家会快速回复的公司。

lines.t: Marketing departments today need to follow technological development.
lines.cn: 如今的市场部门需要跟上技术发展。

lines.t: For example, this year’s smartphone is smarter than last year’s; self-driving cars are now on the road.
lines.cn: 例如，今年的智能手机比去年的更聪明；自动驾驶汽车已经上路。

lines.t: Marketers have to do research on which technologies are coming into being.
lines.cn: 营销人员必须研究哪些技术正在出现。

lines.t: Otherwise, they risk being left behind in the virtual dust.
lines.cn: 否则，他们就有在虚拟尘埃中被甩下的风险。

lines.t: Marketing has also changed due to the importance of video.
lines.cn: 营销也因视频的重要性而改变。

lines.t: People don’t just want to read text; they want to watch things happening.
lines.cn: 人们不只想读文字；他们想看事情发生。

lines.t: Companies now have to explore how they can use video on a consistent basis to share information about their businesses.
lines.cn: 公司现在必须探索如何持续运用视频来分享有关自身业务的信息。

lines.t: Fortunately, it’s extremely easy to shoot something these days.
lines.cn: 幸运的是，如今拍东西极其容易。

lines.t: All you need is a smartphone.
lines.cn: 你只需要一部智能手机。

lines.t: But what’s the result of all this?
lines.cn: 但这一切带来了什么结果？

lines.t: Shorter attention spans.
lines.cn: 注意力持续时间更短。

lines.t: We aren’t the same people that we were 20 years ago.
lines.cn: 我们已不再是 20 年前的我们。

lines.t: Not only have we grown accustomed to getting the information we want instantaneously, our attention spans are much shorter.
lines.cn: 我们不仅习惯了即时获得想要的信息，注意力持续时间也短得多。

lines.t: If something doesn’t capture our attention within a few seconds, we’re on to the next piece of content.
lines.cn: 如果某样东西没能在几秒内抓住我们的注意力，我们就转向下一条内容。

lines.t: Marketers need to figure out ways to speak directly to the customers’ emotions, and they need to figure out how to do that as quickly as possible.
lines.cn: 营销人员需要找到直接诉诸顾客情感的办法，而且需要尽快做到。

lines.t: Once people are emotionally engaged, they’ll stick with you.
lines.cn: 一旦人们在情感上被吸引，他们就会一直跟着你。

lines.t: If marketing has changed this much in the past 20 years, imagine what the next 20 years will bring.
lines.cn: 如果营销在过去 20 年变化如此之大，想象一下未来 20 年会带来什么。

lines.t: In a recent survey, only 9% of marketers could say with confidence that their marketing efforts were actually working.
lines.cn: 在最近一项调查中，只有 9% 的营销人员能自信地说自己的营销努力确实有效。

lines.t: Their confidence is being shaken, because the rules of the game change every year.
lines.cn: 他们的信心正被动摇，因为游戏规则每年都在变。

lines.t: That’s why it’s important for marketers to pay attention to the latest technological developments and consider collaborating with technological innovators.
lines.cn: 正因如此，营销人员必须关注最新技术发展，并考虑与技术革新者合作。

lines.t: That way, they’ll be moving at the same pace as the tech industry.
lines.cn: 这样，他们就能与技术行业步调一致地前进。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 7 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say is interesting?

options.A: People have only one social engagement per week.
options.B: Working together enhances friendship.
options.C: Few people have devoted friends.
options.D: Friendships benefit work.

questions.cn: 讲话者说什么很有意思？

optionsCn.A: 人们每周只参加一次社交活动。
optionsCn.B: 一起工作会增进友谊。
optionsCn.C: 很少有人有忠实的朋友。
optionsCn.D: 友谊有益于工作。

questions.stem: What did researchers from an American university analyze in their initial study?

options.A: The impact of friends on people’s self-esteem.
options.B: How supportive friends can be in the workplace.
options.C: How to boost one’s sense of value and worthiness.
options.D: The role of family ties in people’s mental well-being.

questions.cn: 一所美国大学的研究者在初步研究中分析了什么？

optionsCn.A: 朋友对人们自尊的影响。
optionsCn.B: 支持性的朋友在职场上能起多大作用。
optionsCn.C: 如何提升个人的价值感。
optionsCn.D: 家庭纽带在人们心理健康中的作用。

questions.stem: What did the second study find about non-work friends?

options.A: They show little interest in their friends’ work.
options.B: They tend to be much more difficult to make.
options.C: They are more trustworthy and reliable.
options.D: They increase people’s job satisfaction.

questions.cn: 第二项研究关于非工作圈的朋友发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们对朋友的工作没什么兴趣。
optionsCn.B: 他们往往更难交到。
optionsCn.C: 他们更值得信任和依靠。
optionsCn.D: 他们提高了人们的工作满意度。

questions.stem: What does the speaker suggest managers do?

options.A: Allow employees to have a flexible work schedule.
options.B: Encourage employees to be friends with colleagues.
options.C: Help employees balance work and family responsibilities.
options.D: Organize activities to nourish friendships outside of work.

questions.cn: 讲话者建议管理者做什么？

optionsCn.A: 允许员工弹性安排工作时间。
optionsCn.B: 鼓励员工与同事交朋友。
optionsCn.C: 帮助员工平衡工作与家庭责任。
optionsCn.D: 组织活动以滋养工作之外的友谊。

lines.t: You might be surprised to learn that the benefits of friendships extend beyond people’s social life and into their work.
lines.cn: 你可能会惊讶地发现，友谊的好处超出人们的社交生活，延伸到了工作中。

lines.t: This is interesting when considering the extent to which people sacrifice friendships, or at least the time they spend with friends, because of the extended hours they’re devoting to work.
lines.cn: 考虑到人们为工作投入更长的时间而牺牲友谊、至少是牺牲与朋友相处的时间的程度，这一点很有意思。

lines.t: Just last week, I was remarking to a colleague that I’m content with only one social engagement per week.
lines.cn: 就在上周，我还跟一位同事说，我一周只参加一次社交活动就很满足。

lines.t: But according to recent research, that’s evidently not enough.
lines.cn: 但根据近期研究，这显然不够。

lines.t: In an initial study of more than 700 respondents, scholars from an American university analyzed the impact that friends, as opposed to family, have on self-esteem and well-being.
lines.cn: 在一项有 700 多名受访者参与的初步研究中，一所美国大学的学者分析了朋友（相对于家人）对自尊和幸福感的影响。

lines.t: Friends came out substantially on top.
lines.cn: 朋友明显胜出。

lines.t: That’s because to be someone’s mate is a voluntary act, unlike family who people rarely get to choose.
lines.cn: 这是因为成为某人的朋友是一种自愿行为，不像家人，人们很少能选择。

lines.t: The researchers found that when people choose to cultivate and maintain supportive friendships with an individual, it means that the person is valued and worthy of their limited time.
lines.cn: 研究者发现，当一个人选择去培养并维持与某个人的支持性友谊时，就意味着这个人被看重、值得占用其有限的时间。

lines.t: Such sentiments of value and worthiness boost our self-esteem.
lines.cn: 这种被看重、值得的价值感会提升我们的自尊。

lines.t: The second study comprised more than 300 participants.
lines.cn: 第二项研究包含 300 多名参与者。

lines.t: It proved that the better we feel about ourselves, the more likely we’ll perform our job confidently and competently.
lines.cn: 它证明：我们对自己感觉越好，就越可能自信而胜任地完成工作。

lines.t: This follow-up study found that non-work friends even improve people’s job satisfaction.
lines.cn: 这项后续研究发现，非工作圈的朋友甚至能提高人的工作满意度。

lines.t: They have as much of an impact on how much they love their jobs as do the friends they have at work, despite not actually being at our place of work.
lines.cn: 尽管他们其实并不在我们工作的地方，但他们对“我们有多爱自己的工作”的影响，与工作中的朋友一样大。

lines.t: These types of friends tend to be our preferred outlet for venting about work-related matters.
lines.cn: 这类朋友往往是我们倾诉工作相关事宜的首选出口。

lines.t: This is an avenue that may not be available at the office.
lines.cn: 这是办公室里可能没有的一条渠道。

lines.t: So even though friendships can be easy to neglect when confronted by pressures at work, or even pressures at home, neglecting our friends can turn out to be harmful and counterproductive.
lines.cn: 所以，尽管面对工作、甚至家庭压力时友谊容易被忽视，但忽视朋友最终可能有害且适得其反。

lines.t: That’s why, when determining how to create a better work-life balance, we need to consider not only how to balance work and family demands, but also how to cultivate and sustain supportive friendships.
lines.cn: 正因如此，在决定如何实现更好的工作与生活平衡时，我们不仅要考虑如何平衡工作与家庭的需求，还要考虑如何培养并维系支持性的友谊。

lines.t: It’s for this reason that managers should never discriminate when it comes to requests from employees for flexible work arrangements.
lines.cn: 也正因如此，管理者在员工提出弹性工作安排请求时，绝不应区别对待。

lines.t: It’s irrelevant whether their need for a desired schedule is due to, say, parenting responsibilities, or a craving to hang out with a best mate.
lines.cn: 他们需要理想作息的理由是育儿责任，还是想和最要好的朋友一起玩，都不重要。

lines.t: What matters is the opportunity to engage in a nourishing activity outside of work.
lines.cn: 重要的是有机会从事一项工作之外的滋养性活动。

lines.t: That will definitely have a follow-on effect at work.
lines.cn: 这肯定会在工作中产生连带效应。
